                                               ORDER


         This matter is before the Court on Plaintiffs Motion for Entry of a Scheduling Order and,

  as Necessary, an Initial Pretrial Conference (ECF _). The Court has considered the Motion, the

  memorandum, and any response and reply.

         It is hereby ORDERED that the Motion is GRANTED as follows.

          1.     A scheduling conference under Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b)(l)(B) and Local Civil Rule

  16(B) is set for - - - -, 2026, at          , before _ _ _ _ , [in Courtroom_/ by telephone

  or video].

         2.      Under Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(±)(1), 26(±)(4), and Local Civil Rule 26(A)(l), the

  parties shall confer under Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(±) no later than seven days before the conference. The

  parties shall file a written Rule 26(±) report no later than three days before the conference. The

  report may state agreed positions and separately identified positions of each party on each subject

  in Rule 26(f)(3). Agreement on every subject is not a condition of entry of the scheduling order.

  Oral reporting at the conference is permitted only if the Court, by further order, excuses the written

  report.

            3.    If a Rule 26(f) report is filed before the conference and the Court determines that

  the report is sufficient, the Court may enter the scheduling order on the report and vacate the

  conference.

            4.    The Court shall enter the scheduling order at the conference or within seven days

  after it. The scheduling order shall limit the time to join other parties, amend the pleadings,

  complete discovery, and file motions, Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b)(3)(A), and shall fix the discovery cut-

  off, the date of the final pretrial conference, and, where practicable, the trial date, Local Civil Rule

  16(B).

            5.    This Order directs conference preparation. It makes no finding concerning any

  party's participation in the Rule 26(f) process to date.

            6.    Nothing in this Order adjudicates the pending objections or applications

  concerning ECF 84 or ECF 96, and no such request is withdrawn by the Motion.

            It is SO ORDERED.
